# .github/doctrine-drift-allowlist.txt
#
# Allowlist for the CI "Doctrine drift scan" step in .github/workflows/ci-validate.yml.
#
# Format: one file path per line, relative to repo root. Comments start with '#'.
# A match (grep hit of the forbidden routing markers — ai-solutions.store,
# CharityRouter100, 60/30/10, 100% to charity — in apps/youandinotai-frontend/
# or backend/fastapi-app/app/) is treated as a passing warning IF the file path
# appears in this list. Any hit in a file NOT in this list fails CI.
#
# This file is the explicit, Josh-visible backlog of pre-existing references
# that need to be triaged: removed, narrowed, or accepted as legitimate
# internal-ops cross-references with the doctrine blocker scope updated.
#
# When the scan is FIXED on 2026-05-17 (PR — restores the broken drift scan
# that had been silently passing since `youandinotai-api/app/` was removed
# from the layout), pre-existing `ai-solutions.store` references in
# apps/youandinotai-frontend/ remain. None are explicit donation/charity
# routing claims — they are cross-references to the AI-Solutions Store
# public surface from neighbouring surfaces. The 2026-07-03 FastAPI target
# restore surfaced the authenticated marketing referral kit's matching
# cross-surface destination list in backend/fastapi-app/app/routers/marketing.py.
# The doctrine blocker, as currently written in CLAUDE.md, lists
# `ai-solutions.store` as a banned string in apps/youandinotai-frontend/
# (lane separation rule).
#
# Triage options for Josh (tracked in awaiting-josh issue — see PR body):
#   A. Remove the cross-references entirely (strict lane separation).
#   B. Narrow the doctrine blocker scope to customer-rendered code only
#      (so internal ops/monitoring/boundary pages are exempt).
#   C. Keep the blocker as-is and update each call-site to a routing-safe
#      indirection (e.g. fetch the surface list from a server-side config).
#
# Removing a file from this list (i.e. fixing the underlying reference)
# tightens the safety net. Adding a new entry MUST be accompanied by a PR
# comment explaining why it is operationally necessary.
